name: product-gap-registry
purpose: Track user-request coverage, deferred product slices, and release gates for the installable desktop agent platform so unfinished work cannot be hidden behind completed feature architecture.

reader_guide.summary: This registry is the durable product gap ledger for the desktop agent platform. It records which recent user requests are covered, partial, or still missing as product slices.
how_to_read: Start with coverage_summary to see whether the user's latest desktop-agent-platform goals are fully closed.
Read request_coverage to map each user request ID to implemented evidence and remaining gap IDs.
Read gap_items before planning new desktop work; p0_product_gap items should be implemented before cosmetic or monitoring-heavy work.
Treat external_release_gate items as release blockers rather than UI feature work.
update_triggers: A user asks whether deferred or missing work remains.
A p0 or p1 desktop product slice is implemented, descoped, or superseded.
Product feature architecture, installer runtime contract, data format, workspace host, or release readiness changes.
Public distribution readiness changes, including signing, notarization, updater, or clean-machine smoke tests.

reference_links.title: Structured user request summaries for 2026-06-03
used_for: Define the request IDs audited by this registry.
Map product gaps back to the user's stated desktop app and agent-platform goals.

reference_links.title: Desktop agent platform product feature registry
used_for: Confirm the intended primary product and feature layer roles.
Separate primary work surfaces from supporting observability.

reference_links.title: Installer shell runtime contract
used_for: Confirm that the installed app owns runtime rules, enforcement gates, and data accumulation targets.
Identify whether a gap is runtime-contract, UI, data, or release-readiness work.

reference_links.title: NIST SP 800-53 SA-11 Developer Testing and Evaluation
used_for: External check that meaningful software work should preserve testing and evaluation evidence.
Support keeping validation handles beside product gap records.

reference_links.title: Atlassian Agile backlog refinement guidance
used_for: External check that deferred work should remain explicit, prioritized, and periodically reviewed.
Support treating missing product slices as backlog items with acceptance criteria rather than chat-only notes.

structure_rules.rule: Every audited user request must have one request_coverage entry with evidence and remaining_gap_ids.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked to re-evaluate whether any requested work was missed.

structure_rules.rule: Gap IDs are stable lower snake_case identifiers and must not be renamed without updating request_coverage and traceability records.
structure_rules.reason: Stable IDs let readiness tests and future audits detect stale or silently removed gaps.

structure_rules.rule: p0_product_gap items should be implemented before new cosmetic UI changes or monitoring-heavy additions.
structure_rules.reason: The user's product goal is agent orchestration, work environment, development environment, agent factory, and learning improvement, not monitoring polish.

structure_rules.rule: External distribution gates stay open until validated with the required external assets and smoke tests.
structure_rules.reason: Public macOS or Windows readiness cannot be claimed without signing, notarization or equivalent packaging validation, updater planning, and clean-machine checks.

field_guide.meaning: Bounded source inventory, exclusions, and audited request range used for this review.
Human-readable count of covered, partial, missing, and externally blocked areas.
One row per audited user request with implemented evidence and remaining gap IDs.
Prioritized unresolved, partial, structural, test, or external release gaps.
Concrete conditions that must be true before a gap can be marked covered.

source_inventory_method: rg --files with local-only and generated output exclusions
Targeted review of _history/user-requests, _history/request-traces, platform-desktop-app/specs, platform-desktop-app/configs, readiness tests, and representative runtime/UI source files
Search for deferred, remaining, Agent Factory, learning loop, PTY, Monaco, workspace host, and release gate terms

coverage_summary.headline: The desktop shell, source workbench, installer runtime contract, data accumulation, workspace host, folder restructure, feature registry, operator separation, Agent Factory proposal wizard, and learning feedback decision loop are implemented internal product slices. Remaining gaps are structural debt, native Git depth, clipboard QA, optional PTY UX, and external public distribution gates.

covered_evidence: Desktop shell with titlebar, activity rail, sidebar, content viewport, settings dialog, task timeline, and decision inbox
Operator Center separation and user/customer view sections
request_coverage.notes: The app is no longer a one-screen web dashboard, but the main renderer shell remains too large and some desktop-native interactions are still typed-form based.

covered_evidence: Monaco Editor integration for code viewing/editing instead of bundling the full VS Code product
Copy Current, multi-file draft queue, diff review, save/revert flows
request_coverage.notes: The code editing capability is implemented; browser-level clipboard success remains a QA gap because permissions can block automation.

request_coverage.notes: Internal product posture is corrected; public distribution remains externally gated.

gap_items.why_it_matters: The user asked for easy agent creation and automatic agent generation as a primary product capability. The Agents surface now guides a user through creating a bounded proposal before promotion into durable agent assets.
current_evidence: platform-desktop-app/configs/product-feature-registry.json includes agent_factory as a primary layer
platform-desktop-app/renderer/workspace-monitor/components/features/ProductFeatureArchitecturePanel.tsx includes Agent Factory cards
agent-platform/configs/orchestration/capability-promotion-registry.json exists as a backend/config foundation
platform-desktop-app/renderer/workspace-monitor/components/MonitorShell.tsx includes AgentFactoryWizard and create_agent_factory_proposal invocation
platform-desktop-app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs implements create_agent_factory_proposal and writes app_data/runtime-data/agent-factory/proposals records
platform-desktop-app/runtime-contracts/installer-shell-runtime-contract.json declares agent_factory_proposals and agent_factory_commands
Readiness tests verify the wizard UI, command surface, and accumulated data store tokens
acceptance_to_close: Desktop Agent Factory view creates or drafts an agent from goal, role, tools, guardrails, validation, and output contract inputs.
Wizard writes a bounded agent proposal into the app-data runtime store with target project path, traceability, and rollback metadata.
Readiness/test verifies the wizard route, generated schema fields, validation command, and customer-safe UI behavior.
Request trace for UR-2026-06-03-035 marks this gap closed with verification evidence.

gap_items.why_it_matters: The user asked for a platform that continuously learns and improves performance. The Agents surface now derives improvement candidates from accumulated data and records human-governed decisions into the runtime store.
current_evidence: Accumulated Data surface and versioned runtime data index exist
Product feature registry marks Learning & Evaluation Loop as primary
Capability promotion registry and evaluation records exist as foundations
platform-desktop-app/renderer/workspace-monitor/components/MonitorShell.tsx includes LearningFeedbackLoopPanel and record_learning_improvement_decision invocation
platform-desktop-app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs implements record_learning_improvement_decision and writes app_data/runtime-data/learning-feedback/decisions records
platform-desktop-app/runtime-contracts/installer-shell-runtime-contract.json declares learning_feedback_decisions and learning_feedback_commands
Readiness tests verify candidate and decision-recording UI, command surface, and accumulated data store tokens
acceptance_to_close: Desktop UI shows improvement candidates generated from task run outcomes, omissions, evaluations, and timing records.
User can approve, reject, defer, or promote a candidate into a prompt, workflow, tool, skill, agent, or product feature.
Approved improvement records link to source evidence, validation, rollback or disablement plan, and post-change evaluation.
Readiness/test verifies candidate ingestion and decision recording.

gap_items.why_it_matters: The app owns workspace import/clone state, but desktop users still need native selection and full Git workflows for the clone-and-work model to feel built-in.
current_evidence: get_desktop_workspace_state, set_desktop_workspace_path, and clone_desktop_workspace are implemented
Workspace Host panel exposes text-path import and clone controls
Source editor and CLI use app-selected workspace first
acceptance_to_close: Native folder picker is available for workspace import.
Git branch, status, commit, pull, push, and conflict state are visible as desktop workbench actions.
Credential and SSH key behavior is documented and guarded by the sensitive-file boundary policy.
Clean workspace smoke test proves import/clone/source/CLI handoff.
blocked_by: credential UX/security decision for private remotes

gap_items.why_it_matters: The UI now behaves more like a desktop workbench, but MonitorShell is still a large component. Future feature work will be slower and riskier if shell, dialogs, panels, and workbench surfaces stay merged.
current_evidence: Desktop shell, settings dialog, runtime panel, source workbench, operator center, and product panels are present
Request traces explicitly name MonitorShell component split as remaining structural work
acceptance_to_close: Split DesktopShell, SidebarNavigation, OverviewHome, SettingsDialog, DesktopRuntimePanel, SourceWorkbench, and OperatorCenter ownership into separate components or modules.
No UI behavior regression in check/test/build/customer snapshot/perf.
Readiness test verifies key component entry points instead of only MonitorShell token scanning.

gap_items.why_it_matters: A PTY/xterm surface can make CLI sessions feel more like a full desktop developer app, but the current bounded pipe-first supervisor is intentionally safer for task-run persistence and decision capture.
current_evidence: start_cli_adapter_session, poll_cli_adapter_session, stdin, defer, cancel, task pipe, and task run store exist
Historical tasks kept interactive PTY supervisor as a follow-up
acceptance_to_close: Product decision chooses whether PTY is required or optional.
If required, install audit records xterm.js/PTY dependency scope, license, rollback, and validation.
PTY lifecycle passes resource guard checks for process, file descriptor, timer, and log retention cleanup.
blocked_by: product decision on terminal UX risk versus pipe-first orchestration

gap_items.why_it_matters: Code copy exists in the UI, but browser automation could not fully prove clipboard success under restricted permissions.
current_evidence: Copy Current and Copy Patch Context actions exist
Browser render verification covered Monaco presence but not successful clipboard write
acceptance_to_close: Add deterministic unit-level clipboard abstraction tests or Tauri clipboard command verification.
Record manual or automated smoke evidence for copy success in the desktop runtime.

gap_items.why_it_matters: The product can be internally built and validated, but public macOS/Windows readiness cannot be honestly claimed without signing, notarization or equivalent verification, update/rollback, and clean-machine smoke tests.
current_evidence: service-readiness registry marks signed distribution and update/recovery as public blockers
macOS execution profile separates developer local run, internal test app, and public distribution
acceptance_to_close: Developer ID or equivalent signing assets are available and recorded without exposing secrets.
Hardened runtime, notarization, stapling where applicable, installer/uninstaller, update/rollback, and clean-machine workspace smoke tests pass.
Release readiness report changes from public_release_blocked to the appropriate release state with evidence.
